When you see a cold front moving in, it can bring changes in the weather. Imagine you have a big, warm blanket covering the sky. This blanket is like a warm air mass. As this blanket moves over a cooler area, it starts to rise up into the air. This rising blanket of warm air can cause clouds to form and even bring rain.

But the rising blanket of warm air isn't alone. It's being pushed by a stronger, cooler air mass, like a cooler blanket. This cooler blanket moves in from somewhere else and pushes the warm blanket up into the sky. As the warm air rises, it cools and condenses into clouds. This is why you might see clouds gathering and the temperature dropping when a cold front comes through.
